Items.Name: Stone
Items.Description: A small, ordinary stone. Good for knapping, campfires and much else; it may break when knapped.

Items.Name: Big rock
Items.Description: A large, heavy rock. Stones can be knapped against it without it breaking.

Items.Name: Small stick
Items.Description: A branch about as thick as your thumb. Kindling, fuel, traps and hand tools.

Items.Name: Big stick
Items.Description: A limb about as thick as your wrist. Firewood, heavier tools and building.

Items.Name: Log
Items.Description: Part of a tree trunk, washed up or fallen. Heavy, and good for building.

Items.Name: Seaweed
Items.Description: A rubbery tangle of seaweed. Edible, and its fibers make basic cordage.

Items.Name: Coconut
Items.Description: A coconut in its husk. Food and water, if you can get at them; too much will upset your stomach.

Items.Name: Palm frond
Items.Description: A long, fallen palm leaf. Good for weaving baskets, bedding and shelter.

Items.Name: Seashell
Items.Description: A small, ridged shell. Pretty, and crushes into a calcium-rich powder.

Items.Name: Crab
Items.Description: A crab scuttling across the sand. Delicious, better cooked; it spoils quickly once caught.

Items.Name: Lobster
Items.Description: A lobster, rarer than crabs. Delicious cooked, but best not eaten raw. It spoils quickly.

Items.Name: Conch
Items.Description: A heavy spiral shell. There may be something edible inside.

Items.Name: Clam
Items.Description: A closed clam. It may hold something edible, and very rarely a pearl.

Items.Name: Oyster
Items.Description: A rough, closed oyster. It may hold something edible, and very rarely a pearl.

Items.Name: Gooseneck barnacle
Items.Description: A rare delicacy clinging to the rocks. You will need a sharp tool to harvest it.

Items.Name: Coral
Items.Description: A piece of dried, brittle coral. Not much use except crushed.

Items.Name: Driftwood
Items.Description: Sun-bleached, crooked wood. Splits into sticks, or makes a crude shield.

Items.Name: Bone
Items.Description: A weathered bone. Ground into bone meal, or shaped into tools.

Items.Name: Feather
Items.Description: A gull feather, gray and white. Fletching, bedding, kindling.

Items.Name: Cone snail
Items.Description: A beautiful patterned shell. You have heard these are very, very dangerous. Best to leave it alone.
Items.FoundWarning: You've heard cone snails are very, very dangerous. Best to leave them alone.

Items.Name: Sea sponge
Items.Description: A dried, brittle sponge. It soaks up liquids and helps with washing and cleaning wounds.

Items.Name: Sand dollar
Items.Description: A flat, round shell with a five-petaled pattern. Inedible; crushes into powder.
